newsitem.title: USA: Radar glitches at Washington's National Airport.
newsitem.headline: Radar glitches at Washington's National Airport.

text.p: The new control tower at Washington D.C.'s National Airport has suffered radar equipment outages on nearly a dozen occasions since it opened on April 5, according to Federal Aviation Administration records, Friday's Washington Post reported.

The radar problems -- which involve aging equipment moved into the tower until a more modern system takes over in four years -- are among a series of technical glitches that have plagued the $25 million tower, the Post says.
Radar problems have included malfunctioning keyboards and power sources and faulty displays that tell controllers an aircraft's speed and altitude.
There were no delays or safety problems because of any of the outages, FAA spokeswoman Arlene Salac told the Post.
"Our facilities people are there and we've brought in people ... to take each scope and try to solve these problems," she was quoted as saying.
National, the nation's 36th-busiest airport, serves about 45,000 passengers a day and handles more than 300,000 flightds a year.
